games.reason: Both chains lack evidence of TF occupancy at the variant, and the ChIP-seq records do not count against either chain: XBP1 was assayed elsewhere without a reported peak, while CREB3L4 was not assayed (E12, E25, E26). The evidence modestly favors XBP1 because it is more highly expressed in MCF7 and its mapped model predicts a stronger ref-over-alt binding difference than the CREB3 model for CREB3L4. These are indirect, in-vitro binding predictions, not proof of cellular binding or a regulatory mechanism.

XBP1 is more directly supported in the MCF7 context: it is reported at 636.6 TPM, versus 48.8 TPM for CREB3L4 (E13, E14). Both TFs have their own mapped QBiC-SELEX models predicting stronger ref-allele binding, and neither has a reported peak at the variant, so binding and occupancy do not otherwise separate the chains. The XBP1 assay and CREB3L4 ChIP rows that were not tested in MCF7 provide no contrary evidence (E25, E26).
